---

## 1. Toggle Button CSS & Properties

**File:** [formats/components/src/components/button/button.css](formats/components/src/components/button/button.css#L524-L527)

```css
&.-toggle[aria-pressed="true"] {
  background: var(--instui-color-background-interactive-action-secondary-active);
  border-color: var(--instui-color-stroke-interactive-action-secondary-active);
  color: var(--instui-color-text-interactive-action-secondary-base);
}
```

**Custom properties referenced:**
- `--instui-color-background-interactive-action-secondary-active`
- `--instui-color-stroke-interactive-action-secondary-active`
- `--instui-color-text-interactive-action-secondary-base`

**Comparison to other button colors:**
- **Primary** (default): Uses `--instui-color-background-interactive-action-primary-*` which resolve to `--instui-primitive-color-blue-blue100/120`
- **Secondary**: Uses `--instui-color-background-interactive-action-secondary-*` which resolve to `--instui-primitive-color-grey-grey10/20`
- **Tertiary**: Uses component-level variables (ghost tokens)

---

## 2. Custom Theme Colors Plugin — How It Works

**File:** [plugins/pantoken/custom-theme-colors/src/index.ts](plugins/pantoken/custom-theme-colors/src/index.ts)

**Plugin mechanism:**
- Emits scoped `:root[data-pantoken-color="…"]` CSS rules for 13 color namespaces: `navy`, `blue`, `green`, `red`, `orange`, `grey`, `plum`, `violet`, `stone`, `sky`, `honey`, `sea`, `aurora`
- **Remapping scope** (lines 128–146):
  - Rewrites `--instui-primitive-color-navy-navy10` through `navy200` → `var(--instui-primitive-color-{selected-scale}-{selected-scale}10)` etc.
  - Rewrites `--instui-primitive-color-blue-blue10` through `blue200` → `var(--instui-primitive-color-{selected-scale}-{selected-scale}10)` etc.
  - **Only navy and blue primitives are remapped — not grey**

**Preservation list** (lines 56–83):
- `PRESERVED_BLUE_ACCENT_TOKENS` array: 33 tokens with explicit "blue" in name (accents, charts, avatars, navigation)
- `STATUS_INTENT_TOKEN` regex (`/^--instui-color-(?:background(?:-pastel)?|stroke|text|icon)-(?:info|success|warning|error)$/u`): Preserves semantic status colors

**Critical gap:** Secondary action tokens (`--instui-color-background-interactive-action-secondary-*`) are **neither** blue-accent tokens **nor** status-intent tokens, and they resolve to **grey** primitives, so they never get rewritten.

**Key function:**
```ts
export function customThemeColorsCss(tokens?: readonly Token[] | Map<string, string>): string {
  // ... lines 103–146 build remapping rules for PRIMITIVE_STEPS [10, 20, ..., 200]
  // Only overwrites navy/blue primitives, preserves blue accents + status intents
}
```

**See also:** [plugins/pantoken/custom-theme-colors/README.md](plugins/pantoken/custom-theme-colors/README.md) — states: "Custom color selection remaps brand primitives only. Explicitly blue accents and semantic status intents retain their source-theme values."

---

## 3. Token Resolution Chain

**Token manifests source:** [tools/upstream-diff/baseline/manifest.json](tools/upstream-diff/baseline/manifest.json) (generated from upstream `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens`)

**Secondary button token resolution:**
- `--instui-color-background-interactive-action-secondary-active` → `--instui-primitive-color-grey-grey20`
- `--instui-color-stroke-interactive-action-secondary-active` → `--instui-primitive-color-grey-grey40`
- `--instui-color-text-interactive-action-secondary-base` → `--instui-primitive-color-grey-grey150`

**Primary button token resolution (for comparison):**
- `--instui-color-background-interactive-action-primary-active` → `--instui-primitive-color-blue-blue120`
- `--instui-color-background-interactive-action-primary-base` → `--instui-primitive-color-blue-blue100`

**Tertiary uses component-level aliases**, not primitives directly (e.g., `--instui-component-base-button-primary-ghost-*`)

**Flow:** Upstream token JSON → Core `buildTokens()` → `@pantoken/tokens` static JSON → Plugin `customThemeColorsCss()` reads and rewrites only navy/blue chains

---

## 4. Canvas Theme Editor Implementation

**Theme application file:** [packages/scaffold/templates/canvas-theme-editor/src/main.ts.tmpl](packages/scaffold/templates/canvas-theme-editor/src/main.ts.tmpl)

**How theme color is applied:**
1. Line 66–68: Inlines all 13 color override rules into `CUSTOM_THEME_COLORS_CSS`
2. Line 70–72: Injects `<style>` with `CUSTOM_THEME_COLORS_CSS` into `document.head`
3. Line 328–330: User clicks a color button → calls `applyThemeColor(color)` → sets `document.documentElement.dataset.pantokenColor = color`
4. Line 457: Preview iframe sets `data-pantoken-color="${selectedColor}"` on its `<html>` root

**Key invocation:**
```ts
function applyThemeColor(color: PantokenColorNamespace, refresh = true): void {
  selectedColor = color;
  document.documentElement.dataset.pantokenColor = color;  // ← Triggers :root[data-pantoken-color="…"] rules
  const colorButton = [...colorButtons].find((button) => button.dataset.color === color);
  if (colorButton) selectButton(colorButtons, colorButton);
  if (refresh) updatePreview();
}
```

**Demo page:** The theme picker is part of the scaffold template; actual docs site uses `@pantoken/canvas-theme-editor` in [platforms/canvas-theme-editor/src/build-theme.ts](platforms/canvas-theme-editor/src/build-theme.ts#L74–75) which always includes the custom-theme-colors CSS file.

---

## 5. Root Cause Summary

| Aspect | Finding |
|--------|---------|
| **What breaks** | `.instui-button.-toggle[aria-pressed="true"]` always renders grey (from `--instui-primitive-color-grey-grey20`) regardless of selected theme |
| **Why** | Plugin only rewrites `--instui-primitive-color-navy-*` and `blue-*`; secondary tokens use grey primitives (`grey-grey10/20/40/150`) which never get remapped |
| **Design intent** | Plugin documented preservation policy: "remaps brand primitives only" — but secondary buttons were intended to track the primary brand color and should use blue/navy primitives, not grey |
| **Actual vs. intended** | Designer/author likely expected secondary to be a lighter shade of the selected brand color; it's hardcoded grey instead |

---

### Fix Option A: Plugin Expansion (Recommended)
**File:** [plugins/pantoken/custom-theme-colors/src/index.ts](plugins/pantoken/custom-theme-colors/src/index.ts#L128–146)

**Change:** Extend remapping to include `--instui-primitive-color-grey-*` primitives (or add an option to include them).

**Function names to modify:**
- `customThemeColorsCss()` lines 128–146: Add grey remapping logic alongside navy/blue

**Trade-off:** All grey tokens would recolor (including neutral UI elements, which might be intentional).

### Fix Option B: Button-Specific Override
**Files:**
- [formats/components/src/components/button/button.css](formats/components/src/components/button/button.css#L524–527)
- Possibly [packages/core/src/build.ts](packages/core/src/build.ts) or token generation layer

**Change:** Make secondary button toggle use primary/blue primitives instead of grey.

**Function names:** Token generation in upstream or pantoken core `buildTokens()` → component layer aliases

**Trade-off:** Changes semantic intent if grey secondary was intentional; only fixes buttons, not other secondary-colored UI.

### Fix Option C: Plugin Filter/Allowlist
**File:** [plugins/pantoken/custom-theme-colors/src/index.ts](plugins/pantoken/custom-theme-colors/src/index.ts#L52–83)

**Change:** Add `SECONDARY_ACTION_TOKENS` allowlist to `PRESERVED_*` logic (inverted), explicitly remapping only secondary action tokens to brand primitives.

**Trade-off:** Surgical, but adds complexity to preservation policy.

---

To confirm the bug and test a fix:
1. Set `data-pantoken-color="green"` on `<html>`
2. Observe: Toggle button (aria-pressed="true") background stays `grey-grey20` instead of becoming a green shade
3. Compare: Primary button correctly becomes green-based

Fixed in [plugins/pantoken/custom-theme-colors/src/index.ts](plugins/pantoken/custom-theme-colors/src/index.ts).

**Root cause:** in the rebrand theme, upstream flattens the secondary action background/stroke tokens to literal hex with a baked alpha (`#44709f33`, `#44709f26`, `#44709f00`). `customThemeColorsCss()` only rewrote `--instui-primitive-color-navy-*` / `blue-*` *var references*, so literal hex was invisible to it — the pressed toggle stayed navy-blue under every palette. The `text-` token was already a var reference, which is why only the fill looked wrong.

**Change:** added a value-relinking pass — build a reverse `#rrggbb → {family, step}` index from the navy/blue primitives, then rewrite any matching literal in a token value to `var(--instui-primitive-color-{scale}-{scale}{step})`, or `color-mix(in srgb, … {alpha}%, transparent)` when the literal carries alpha. It recurses into both sides of `light-dark()`, handles `#rgb`/`#rgba`/`#rrggbb`/`#rrggbbaa`/`rgb()`/`rgba()`, skips icon data URIs, and skips preserved blue accents and status intents. Beyond the six secondary tokens it also picked up the institutional-brand fill, the shadow colors, and ten `--instui-component-base-button-*` ghost/secondary/tertiary tokens that had the same defect.

I went through the full themeable token set and expanded the demo from 4 sections to 9.

**What I found.** 88 non-primitive tokens resolve from the navy/blue brand scales — far more than the button and shadow tokens the demo covered. - **Links & text** — Link component (sizes, glyph, disabled), links in prose, `.instui-text -color-brand`. Link color comes from the navigation text scale.

1. Icons turned out to be necessary — breadcrumb separators and pagination arrows rendered as broken squares without them. data.content:
You were right — on-color *is* a fixed scale, and that's exactly what broke it.

**What's actually going on:**

The on-color tokens are plain `var()` references with no `light-dark()`:
- `--instui-color-background-interactive-action-primary-on-color-base` → `white`
- `--instui-color-text-interactive-action-primary-on-color-base` → `navy160`
- `--instui-color-stroke-interactive-action-secondary-on-color-base` → `white`
- `--instui-color-text-interactive-navigation-primary-on-color-base` → `white` (the inverse link)

White fills, white borders, dark text — fixed in both schemes, which only works over a **dark** backdrop.

But the surface I had them on, `--instui-color-background-brand`, *is* `light-dark()`:

```css
--instui-color-background-brand: light-dark(
  var(--instui-primitive-color-navy-navy170),
  var(--instui-primitive-color-navy-navy10)
);
```

So in dark mode it flipped from `navy170` to `navy10` — near-white. White-on-near-white. That's the contrast failure you saw; `-background-brand` and the on-color scale simply aren't a compatible pair in dark mode.

**Fix:** the on-color panel now paints from a fixed `--instui-primitive-color-navy-navy170` instead of the light-dark brand token. It still tracks the swatch (the plugin remaps the navy primitives), but it stays dark in both schemes, which is what on-color expects. Verified in both modes with `sea`: dark teal panel, white pill and outlined button, white inverse link.

I also rewrote the section copy to explain the pairing rule rather than implying any brand surface will do.

Worth noting for the design side: section 5's `-background-brand` card is still fine, because it pairs with `--instui-color-text-inverse`, which *is* `light-dark()` and flips along with it. The mismatch is specifically fixed-on-color over a light-dark brand surface — if InstUI intends `-background-brand` to be the canonical on-color backdrop, that's an upstream inconsistency worth raising.
